title: Finite direct sums of finite-presentation modules are finite presentation
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space and $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; being abelian, it is additive, so any two objects have a biproduct [def-weil-additive-category]. Let $\mathcal G,\mathcal H$ be $\mathcal O_X$-modules of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] (every $x\in X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ such that the restriction to $U$ is isomorphic to the cokernel, in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$, of an $\mathcal O_U$-linear map $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}$ with $m,n\in\mathbf N$). Then the biproduct $\mathcal G\oplus\mathcal H$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ is of finite presentation.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PJ (label lemma-directed-colimit-diagram-finite-presentation), proof, first paragraph after the claim: 'Since a direct sum of finitely presented O_X-modules is finitely presented' (asserted without proof); the notion is Modules, Definition 01BN (label definition-finite-presentation, modules.tex)

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$. Choose presentations of $\mathcal G$ on $U_1\ni x$ and $\mathcal H$ on $U_2\ni x$, of ranks $(m_k,n_k)$, using [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation](2). Put $U=U_1\cap U_2$.

source.place: Tag 01PJ, lemma-directed-colimit-diagram-finite-presentation, proof of filteredness at the direct-sum assertion; expanded using Modules Tag 01BN, definition-finite-presentation.

proof.text: Restrict the two presentations to U using SheafOfModules.Presentation.map, the Mathlib realization of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-functor-presentation-transport]. Mathlib overMapPushforwardAdj makes restriction a left adjoint, so it preserves colimits; overMapUnitIso identifies its image of the unit with the unit. The source-library Presentation.isFinite_map shows finiteness since the generator and relation index sets are unchanged. Transport the results along overFunctorMap to obtain finite global presentations of G|U and H|U.

source.place: Tag 01PJ, lemma-directed-colimit-diagram-finite-presentation, proof of filteredness at the direct-sum assertion; expanded using Modules Tag 01BN, definition-finite-presentation.

proof.text: The restriction functor overFunctor is additive and preserves finite colimits (Mathlib restriction adjunction, also supplied by the existing moduleOverFunctor instances). Functor.mapBiprod gives (G ⊕ H)|U ≅ G|U ⊕ H|U. This is the canonical comparison from the biproduct universal property [def-weil-additive-category] in the module-sheaf categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tag 01PJ, lemma-directed-colimit-diagram-finite-presentation, proof of filteredness at the direct-sum assertion; expanded using Modules Tag 01BN, definition-finite-presentation.

proof.text: Apply the already proved source-library construction SheafOfModules.Presentation.sigma to the two restricted presentations, indexed by the universe-lifted walking pair. It constructs the coproduct presentation by taking coproducts of the generator and relation maps and using the cokernel universal property; the free-sheaf comparison identifies the generators and relations with the disjoint unions of the original index sets. Presentation.isFinite_sigma proves this presentation finite, since the index family and the supplied generator and relation sets are finite [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. This directly realizes the block-diagonal construction without the separate unproved binary cokernel lemma.

source.place: Tag 01PJ, lemma-directed-colimit-diagram-finite-presentation, proof of filteredness at the direct-sum assertion; expanded using Modules Tag 01BN, definition-finite-presentation.

proof.text: Sigma.reindex removes the universe lift from the two-element index set, and biprod.isoCoprod identifies the resulting binary coproduct with G|U ⊕ H|U [def-weil-additive-category]. Presentation.ofIsIso transports the finite presentation across this isomorphism. Presentation.isFinitePresentation gives local finite presentation, then transport along the comparison of Step 3 and apply IsFinitePresentation.of_coversTop to the intersection cover. This proves the claim by [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], including empty spaces and zero generator or relation ranks.
